clue.text: See jazz group going round Asian capital

indicators.note: the jazz group goes round, enclosing the word for see

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz band
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a jazz band touring an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital and largest city of Sri Lanka, in South Asia.

clue.text: Former head of English entered punctually

indicators.note: the leading letter goes into the phrase for punctually

parts.note: punctually means on time

indicators.note: head of signals the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A former boss of the English department always arrived on the dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-time holder of a post is a former one: the hyphenated adjective means erstwhile.

clue.text: Ready to start acting from the beginning

definitions.meaning: an actor who is on the set is in place to begin performing
the start or commencement of something

explanation.surface: An actor primed to perform from the very first scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is where a film actor stands to work; as one word it means the start of something.

clue.text: Slip in a pound raised subject to control

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
under, as in under control, means subject to it

explanation.surface: A slip in a currency that was raised while under tight control.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a careless mistake, a slip.

clue.text: Very involved psychological state

explanation.surface: A very involved state of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means intricate; as a noun it is a psychological fixation.

clue.text: Insult by leaving a tip

parts.note: off means departing, as in we're off
an end, as in the tip of a finger

explanation.surface: Being insulting by walking out without leaving a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, which fits the restaurant surface, but here it is an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to affront or insult them.

clue.text: Jack's screwdriver?

parts.note: Jack is a sailor, and a ship's screw is what drives it through the water

explanation.surface: Asking which tool belongs to a man named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack tar is an old nickname for a sailor; a ship's screw is the device that drives it, so the screwdriver is not a tool at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screw is a rotating bladed device that pushes the vessel forward.

clue.text: Cuts taxes

definitions.meaning: duties levied on goods such as alcohol and tobacco

explanation.surface: A headline about cutting taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cuts out; the noun names duties charged on home-produced goods.

clue.text: New life for an incinerator that's recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving an old incinerator a second life by recycling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges the letters of AN INCINERATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth of a soul in a fresh body is a new life after death.

clue.text: Elizabeth, a superior lady deserted by a sailor

indicators.note: the sailor walks out, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: an abbess is the mother superior of a convent
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Elizabeth, a grand lady abandoned by a seafarer.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AB from ABBESS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bess is a familiar short form of the name, as in Good Queen Bess for Elizabeth I.

clue.text: A chief constable's ultimate deterrent?

parts.note: a chief constable heads a police force, which he might employ as a last resort

explanation.surface: What a senior police officer holds back as a last resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A chief constable heads a British police force, so the phrase also suggests putting that force to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical coercion is the final means of compelling compliance when persuasion fails.

clue.text: Describing Jill when cut off by Edward?

definitions.text: Describing Jill when cut off by Edward?

indicators.note: cut off means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Jill has been dumped by her boyfriend Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: JIL (Jill shortened) followed by TED; the whole clue also describes Jill's state when Ted breaks it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman abruptly dropped by a lover has been jilted.

clue.text: Production of Lear? Don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear wrote comic verse of this kind, such as The Owl and the Pussycat
an exclamation of disbelief, like rubbish!

explanation.surface: Scepticism about a staging of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear here is Edward Lear, the Victorian author of comic verse, not Shakespeare's king.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's Book of Nonsense names his genre, and the same word is a scornful dismissal.

clue.text: Wild-eyed satyr of very recent history

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed mythical satyr from the recent past.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is the most recent past, history only just made.

clue.text: It's not for nothing you pass through them

definitions.text: It's not for nothing you pass through them

parts.words: It's not for nothing you pass through them
parts.note: passage through these barriers costs money, so it is literally not free

explanation.surface: A proverb-like remark about doorways that matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for nothing' usually means with good reason; here it means you must pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Barriers on a road where drivers stop and pay a charge before being let through.

clue.text: The end is nigh!

explanation.surface: A doom-monger's placard announcing the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced one way it means the finish; another way it means near.

clue.text: Some found nervously lying in a cunning way

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Someone nervously telling lies, but craftily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something artfully or with guile is doing it craftily.

clue.text: The Parisian is on river for relaxation

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: le is French for the
taken as written
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A Parisian relaxing on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time spent at ease is leisure, a synonym for relaxation.

clue.text: Type of joint that may be found worldwide

definitions.meaning: a coupling that lets a shaft turn at any angle, as in a car's drive shaft

explanation.surface: A kind of joint found all over the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical joint allowing movement in all directions shares its name with the word meaning global.

clue.text: Wild flower absorbs nitrogen

indicators.note: the flower takes the chemical element into itself

parts.note: a violet is a small purple flower
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A wild flower taking up nitrogen from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild in the sense of fierce and uncontrolled, like a raging storm.

clue.text: Explain about what keeps a wheel on

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to explain the thing holding a wheel in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin through the end of an axle stops the wheel sliding off it.

clue.text: Meal inside the German hotel

indicators.note: the hotel goes inside the German article

parts.note: der is German for the
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: Eating a meal inside a German hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening.

clue.text: Language master demands Latin, initially — and using it in translation!

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it
translating turns words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A master of languages insists on Latin and on translating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' is the anagram signal; the surface makes it sound like the linguist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in several tongues is a master of language.

clue.text: Hidden firm backing religious system

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a cult is a system of religious worship

explanation.surface: A secretive company funding a religious movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means secret or esoteric, knowledge kept from the uninitiated.

clue.text: Penny each, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A shop sign pricing items at a penny apiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges P and EACH; the whole clue also describes a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods costing a penny apiece are inexpensive, low in price.

clue.text: Collar — or another part of the shirt?

definitions.meaning: to collar someone is to seize them and detain them in talk
the slit through which a button is passed

explanation.surface: Choosing between a shirt's collar and some other part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a noun for part of the shirt, but it is a verb: to accost.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to stop and detain them; it is also the slit a button goes through.

clue.text: Spot for parking inside, yes? Possibly

indicators.note: the parking letter goes inside the other letters
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is a parking space inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges YES to ESY, and 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, to descry it.

clue.text: It comes last, locked in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: tressed means having locks or tresses of hair

explanation.surface: Something that comes at the end, jammed in reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked' suggests secured, but it means having locks of hair: TRESSED, turned round by 'in reverse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet course is served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: A living wage?

parts.note: a living is a church benefice, so its pay is a cleric's salary

explanation.surface: A question about pay enough to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England a living is a post held by a vicar or rector, so the wage is a clergyman's.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary paid to a clergyman or other office holder.
